audit.why: 45.33% over 2246 games, and the chart gives Sylas all seven stages — those agree, and the reasons hold up: Chain Lash reaches 775 against Seismic Shard's 625, Kingslayer heals back the chip, and Hijack means Malphite's one win condition can be turned around on him. The full layer's diffRating of 6/10 is the outlier against a 45% lane marked HARD, but the stage-by-stage read is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] frames Hijack as a permanent background threat ('never ult into him with R available') with no timing attached, so the player has no way to know when it is actually available.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s and Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100s. At rank 1 he gets one copy for your one cast; at rank 3 he can copy your ultimate roughly three times for each one you have. That ratio, not a vague warning, is the spike — and it is why the matchup gets worse for Malphite as the game runs long rather than better.
audit.corrected: Hijack: 80s at rank 1, 30s at rank 3, against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100s. Late he copies your engage several times per cast you get.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: the entry never names a single Sylas ability. Every reference is generic — 'W-drain', 'Q magic damage', 'E chain-dash', 'his R'. Kingslayer is also mis-described as a drain-poke he heals off you with.
audit.why: Kingslayer is a 400-range lunge that damages and heals him against champions — a commit tool, not a poke. The poke is Chain Lash at 775 range, which lands, slows, and then detonates a second time out of the intersection point after a delay. Merging the two into one 'W-drain poke' means the player never learns that the damage he is taking at range and the heal he cannot out-chip come off two different buttons on two different cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash (Q) is the 775-range poke on 10s falling to 6s and it hits twice — the lash, then a delayed explosion from the intersection. Kingslayer (W) is a 400-range lunge on 12s falling to 6s that heals him. Abscond/Abduct (E) is the dash with a chain recast. Hijack (R) steals your ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seismic Shard's move-speed steal is mentioned once in passing and never tied to the one thing it is good for here.
audit.why: Sylas has a dash on E and a lunge on W. A move-speed steal on a flat 8s from 625 range does not chase him down — but once both his mobility tools are spent (13s on Abscond at rank 1, 12s on Kingslayer) walking is his only escape, and that is the window the steal actually converts. That is the sequencing the entry lacks.
audit.corrected: Seismic Shard takes his Move Speed for 3s on a flat 8s. It only converts once Abscond's 13s is spent, because that is the only time walking is his escape.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere in the entry, in a matchup whose stated losing condition is that his healing outlasts your chip.
audit.why: Kingslayer heals Sylas against enemy champions, and the entry says three separate times that he 'heals through' the poke war. Grievous Wounds is the answer to exactly that and is never named. _missing-interactions.json flags this pairing for needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is core here, not situational — Kingslayer is what makes the extended trade unwinnable without it.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] calls the first-item stage an 'Even window' and 'a coin-flip', while the chart's win[5] on the same page gives that stage to Sylas.
audit.why: The two are read side by side. One is wrong, and it is not the chart: at 45.33% with Hijack back every 55s and Kingslayer's heal scaling, first item does not even the lane out.
audit.corrected: First item is still his. The honest framing is that this is your best window inside a losing lane, not an even one.

edits.before: Sylas owns the opening — his Q magic damage and W-drain poke you down and heal him back, so your Granite Shield gets chunked off faster than it refreshes and you have no trade pattern to answer. Your only tool here is Q (Seismic Shard) to slow and steal move speed, but one bolt does not stop his sustain. Do not walk up for an auto-trade — his E (chain-dash) closes the gap, stuns, and you eat W-drain damage for free. Last-hit at max range, take the poke, and just survive to Level 6.
edits.after: Sylas owns the opening. Chain Lash (Q) reaches 775 to your 625 and hits twice — the lash, then a delayed explosion out of the intersection point — while Kingslayer (W) heals back whatever you chip, so Granite Shield is stripped faster than it recharges. Seismic Shard steals his Move Speed for 3s on a flat 8s, but one bolt does not beat that sustain. Do not walk up for an auto-trade: Abscond (E) closes the gap on 13s and you eat the lunge for free. Last-hit at max range, take the poke, survive to 6.

edits.before: Level 6 is your single window — Unstoppable Force can flank and knock him up before he reacts, and your E armor-slow blunts his follow-up. But this is a trap if you misplay it: bait out his E chain-dash stun FIRST, because if he has it up he dashes out of your R, and if he has R up he STEALS your Unstoppable Force and flips the engage onto you. Only ult when both his E and R are down, ideally with a jungler. Outside that one all-in, his W-drain still out-sustains your W/E trades.
edits.after: Level 6 is your single window. Unstoppable Force can flank and knock him up before he reacts, and Ground Slam's attack-speed cut blunts the follow-up. It is a trap if you misplay it: bait Abscond FIRST, because with 13s of dash up he simply leaves your R, and with Hijack up he takes Unstoppable Force off you and flips the engage. Commit only when both are down, ideally with a jungler. Outside that all-in, Kingslayer's heal out-sustains anything Thunderclap and Ground Slam produce.

edits.before: This goes the wrong way for you. Sylas is an AP bruiser who out-damages your armor stacking — your W and E both scale off armor, which does nothing against his magic damage, while his W-drain and Q heal through anything you put out. He out-scales a low-economy tank in the straight 1v1, and his R perpetually threatens to steal your Unstoppable Force the moment you engage. Build MR, play for your team's pick rather than a solo duel, and use R as a flank on his carry — not as a 1v1 button into Sylas himself.
edits.after: This goes the wrong way. Chain Lash and Kingslayer are magic damage, so the armour that grows your Ground Slam defends nothing, and Kingslayer heals him through your grind unless you bought Grievous Wounds. Worse, the ratio moves against you: Hijack falls to 30s while Unstoppable Force sits at 100s, so he copies your engage several times over for each one you get. Build MR, play for your team's pick instead of a duel, and land R on his carry — never as a 1v1 button into Sylas.

notes: Packet defect confirmed and fixed: the entry named none of Sylas's abilities. Two substantive corrections beyond naming. (1) Kingslayer was written as a drain-poke he heals off you with; it is a 400-range lunge on 12s falling to 6s. The poke is Chain Lash at 775, which hits twice — the lash plus a delayed explosion out of the intersection point. Collapsing them hid that the damage and the heal are different buttons on different cooldowns. (2) Hijack was a vague standing threat; it is 80/55/30s against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100s, which is the real reason this matchup decays for Malphite instead of improving. Also added Grievous Wounds — flagged in _missing-interactions.json and never mentioned, despite the entry saying three times that he heals through your chip. UNVERIFIED: both layers call Abscond/Abduct a stun. Riot's text says only 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits', and the kit file carries no hardCC flag on it. I left every existing 'stun' reference untouched rather than assert or deny it. FULL LAYER, NOT EDITED: diffRating is 6/10 on a 45.33% lane marked HARD — that reads far easier than the lane is and should be nearer 8/10, but it is an enum-style value that cannot survive the +/-10% band.
